title: Compact-support projection formula at all coefficient stages
statement:
In the six-functor datum of
[def-fix-six-functor-datum], let $f:X\to Y$ be
separated of finite
type, let $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and
$L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, using the
finite-Tor subcategory.
The
projection transformation, built from the
derived tensor and pullback
and the finite-level compact-support direct image of
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] and its higher-coefficient versions
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support],
is then an isomorphism at every coefficient stage:

$$
\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}:Rf_!K\otimes^L_{\Lambda}L
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf_!\bigl(K\otimes^L_{\Lambda}Lf^*L\bigr),
$$

natural in $K$ and $L$, compatible with the composition law of
[thm-sf-comp-composition] (associativity pentagon), with the compactification comparisons, with
finite reduction on the stated finite-Tor domains and scalar extension,
and with the identification
$Rf_!\cong Rf_*$ for proper $f$. At the rational and algebraically closed stages, when $X=X_0\otimes_{k_0}k$, $Y=Y_0\otimes_{k_0}k$ for separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes and $f$ is the geometric base change of a separated finite-type $k_0$-morphism $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$, the isomorphism restricts to the Weil categories [def-wf-weil-category], with tensor as in [def-wf-tensor-product]. A projection formula for the
derived direct image is asserted
only in the proper case, where it is this same statement via
$Rf_!\cong Rf_*$.

proof.text: Use the operation datum [def-fix-six-functor-datum] and fix the projection transformation of [def-exchange-projection]. For a compactification $f=pj$, its component is the projection map of $Rp_*$ at $(j_!K,L)$ followed by $Rp_*$ of $j_!K\otimes^LLp^*L\cong j_!(K\otimes^LLf^*L)$. At finite coefficients $Rf_!^c=Rp_*j_!$ is [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]; at the integral, rational and algebraically closed stages use precisely the completed, localized and common-stage functors of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Thus throughout the proof PF means this specified natural transformation, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism with the same endpoints.

source.place: Proof, first sentence; statement, projection transformation and coefficient stages

proof.text: Let $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], choose bounded constructible etale representatives $K_0,L_0$ with witnesses $\nu_X^*K_0\cong K$, $\nu_Y^*L_0\cong L$. The converse direction of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] transfers the finite Tor interval of $L$ to $L_0$; $L_0$ is bounded below because it is bounded. Now [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula] applies to $f,K_0,L_0$ and its witnessed pro-etale realizations. It says exactly that the component of the transformation in step 1 is invertible and natural in $K,L$. No finite Tor condition on $K$ is needed here.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: finite coefficient formula, with intrinsic pro-etale objects supplied witnesses

proof.text: For $1\le m\le n$, restrict now to $K,L$ both in the finite-Tor domains. The square asserted by [prop-sf-pf-reduction] compares the actual maps $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ and $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K_m,L_m}$, so the isomorphisms of step 2 commute with successive finite reductions. The stronger map-identification information in [lem-fix-operation-reduction] says that coefficient comparisons preserve the tensor associativity, units and counits which construct PF, and also applies from the completed integral stage to each $A_{E,n}$. Consequently these are reduction compatibilities of the specified transformation. This does not assert that finite reduction stays bounded constructible for arbitrary non-finite-Tor $K$.

source.place: Proof, second sentence: successive coefficient reductions

proof.text: Let $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$. By [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor], $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)=D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$, so the given $K$, as well as $L$, satisfies the uniform finite-level Tor condition. Their reductions therefore lie in the domains of step 3. They are derived complete and uniformly bounded in the sense of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Apply the concrete reconstruction assertion of [thm-sf-pf-adic]: the compatible finite components realize the canonical component $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ as an isomorphism, compatible with every finite reduction. The stated conclusion of that node identifies the canonical map itself; no inference that conservative reduction functors are faithful on morphisms is made.

source.place: Proof, third sentence, integral clause; supplies the previously missing finite-Tor hypothesis on K

proof.text: At $E$-coefficients, [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] defines the category as the raw scalar localization of the integral category, with the same objects. Thus choose integral representatives of $K$ and $L$; step 4 applies to those representatives. The concrete coefficient-passage assertion of [thm-sf-pf-field] gives the canonical projection isomorphism over $E$ and its extension compatibilities. At $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] represents both inputs over a common finite extension $E'$. Apply the same assertion of [thm-sf-pf-field] there and take its common-stage image. Its scalar-extension compatibility makes the image independent of the chosen common stage. By [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], at these field stages $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ by definition; no assertion that constructible sheaves are site-perfect is used.

The finite-site realization for arbitrary bounded constructible $K$ has already been established in step 2 by the witnessed clause of [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]. On finite-Tor inputs the realization assertion is also [thm-sf-pf-proetale]. At the integral stage the extra finite-Tor hypothesis on $K$ required by that node was supplied in step 4, and at field stages it is part of the convention recalled in step 5. Thus [thm-sf-pf-proetale] identifies the realizations at all the remaining stages. This uses the completed integral coefficient system and its finite realizations, followed by localization and common stages; it never replaces those coefficient categories with discrete etale $\mathcal O_E$- or $E$-module categories. In particular that finite-Tor realization theorem was not applied to a non-finite-Tor finite-level $K$.

Apply the transformation-identity clauses of [prop-sf-pf-coherence] to the projection transformations fixed in step 1: naturality, the associativity pentagon through $\alpha_{g,f}$, and independence of the compactification give exactly the first compatibility assertions in the statement. At finite coefficients $\alpha_{g,f}$ is the unital associative law of [thm-sf-comp-composition] on bounded-below etale-origin complexes; the representatives of step 2 belong to that domain. At the higher stages it is the composition comparison in the coherence statement, compatible with the finite one under the coefficient comparisons. No higher-coefficient composition theorem is inferred from the finite-level statement of [thm-sf-comp-composition]. The same coherence statement expressly includes finite reduction, scalar extension and pro-etale realization; finite reduction is read only on the finite-Tor domains as in step 3. These are identities for the specified natural transformations; one does not choose separate inverses or unrelated isomorphisms at the different stages.

source.place: Proof, fifth sentence: composition, refinement and coefficient identities

proof.text: If $f$ is proper, use the proper-coincidence clause of [prop-sf-pf-coherence]. It identifies the map in step 1 through $Rf_!\cong Rf_*$ with the direct-image projection transformation. The isomorphism already proved is therefore the direct-image formula in precisely this proper case. This clause provides the asserted compatibility with proper coincidence, rather than postulating a direct-image formula for arbitrary $f$.

For the Weil assertion impose the finite-field model stated in the corrected statement, and let the inputs carry Weil structures. [lem-fix-weil-operations] applies to $f_0$ and its geometric fiber $f$ at $E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$: the underlying operations have their canonical Weil structures on the stated bounded constructible domains and the projection transformation is equivariant. Its tensor structure is the one of [def-wf-tensor-product]. Thus the underlying projection isomorphism is a morphism between the required Weil objects. This is why the finite-field model is required here; it is not a restriction on the non-Weil projection formula proved in the earlier steps.

source.place: Proof, sixth sentence: equivariance for Weil complexes

proof.text: Write $u:S\to T$ for this component and $\varphi_S,\varphi_T$ for its Weil maps. Equivariance says $u\varphi_S=\varphi_T\Phi^*(u)$. Multiply on the left by $u^{-1}$ and on the right by $\Phi^*(u^{-1})$ to obtain $\varphi_S\Phi^*(u^{-1})=u^{-1}\varphi_T$. Hence its underlying inverse is also a Weil morphism, by [def-wf-weil-category]. Therefore the equivariant morphism of step 9 is an isomorphism in the Weil category itself, and its naturality follows from the same naturality equation already used for the underlying transformation.

source.place: Proof, sixth sentence, explicit passage from equivariant underlying isomorphism to Weil isomorphism
